result.title: What Makes a Good Unmasking Policy? A Controlled Study of Learned Unmasking in Diffusion Language Models
result.summary: Masked diffusion language models generate tokens in parallel, but their efficiency depends on which predictions are committed. Learned unmasking policies improve the speed--accuracy trade-off, yet differ in supervision, inputs, and capacity, obscuring which choices matter. We view supervised policies as distilling a decoding procedure through a teacher and examine independently what the teacher labels as committable, on which states the policy imitates it, what the policy observes, and how much the number of function evaluations (NFE) must decrease to offset policy overhead. We find that labeling predictions matching the final output is overly permissive at low NFE, and hidden states are weak alone but can complement confidence. About a 10% NFE reduction suffices to offset policy overhead for policies up to 7.5M parameters across tested settings. We therefore train a policy on trajectory-contraction targets, which accept only commitments staying on a reference trajectory, using confidence and hidden states. On LLaDA-8B-Instruct, the resulting 856K-parameter policy achieves the best accuracy--NFE frontier and highest throughput on GSM8K, is competitive at moderate targets on MATH-500 and HumanEval, and largely transfers to Dream-7B-Instruct.

AI.brief_summary: 系统拆解掩码扩散语言模型中学得 unmasking 策略的有效因素，分别考察监督标签、模仿所用状态、策略输入与容量，并提出只接受停留在参考轨迹上的提交的 trajectory-contraction 训练目标，在 LLaDA-8B 等模型上验证准确率—NFE 前沿。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本并行解码工作，但其「何时可提交/停止」的监督构造、hidden state 与 confidence 互补的发现以及 NFE 收益须抵消策略开销的核算方式，可供核查 LVR 的停止决策与动态计算成本问题。
